canonical_statement: EMPA-KIDNEY was designed to assess whether once-daily empagliflozin reduces progression of kidney disease or cardiovascular disease and to characterize safety in a broad population with chronic kidney disease.
EMPA-KIDNEY was an international randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial.
The trial was conducted at 241 centers in eight countries.
Regulatory authorities and ethics committees at each center approved the trial, and all participants provided written informed consent.
An independent data and safety monitoring committee regularly reviewed unblinded data and conducted a protocol-specified formal interim efficacy analysis.
The steering committee included representatives from the University of Oxford central coordinating office, recruiting regions, the sponsor, and other clinical and statistical experts.

The trial was supported by Boehringer Ingelheim, grants to the University of Oxford from Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly, and public/charitable research funding including the UK Medical Research Council and British Heart Foundation.
The article directs readers to author disclosure forms available with the full text; the writing committee included employees or representatives of Boehringer Ingelheim.
The Nuffield Department of Population Health at the University of Oxford holds the original full trial database, and the article states that a data-sharing statement is available with the full text.
Adults with CKD were eligible if eGFR was at least 20 but less than 45 mL/min/1.73 m², regardless of albuminuria.
Adults with eGFR at least 45 but less than 90 mL/min/1.73 m² were eligible only if urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio was at least 200 mg/g at screening.

population.label: Eligibility criterion
inclusion_criteria: eGFR ≥45 and <90 mL/min/1.73 m² with UACR ≥200 mg/g

canonical_statement: Patients with or without diabetes were eligible.
Participants were expected to receive an appropriate dose of a single-agent renin–angiotensin system inhibitor unless it was not tolerated or not indicated.

population.label: Eligibility criterion
inclusion_criteria: Appropriate single-agent RAS inhibition unless not tolerated or not indicated

canonical_statement: Patients with polycystic kidney disease were excluded.
Patients on maintenance dialysis, with a functioning kidney transplant, or with a scheduled living-donor transplant were excluded.

population.label: Eligibility criterion
exclusion_criteria: Maintenance dialysis, functioning kidney transplant, or scheduled living-donor transplant

canonical_statement: Current treatment with an SGLT2 or SGLT1/2 inhibitor was an exclusion criterion.

population.label: Eligibility criterion
exclusion_criteria: Current SGLT2 or SGLT1/2 inhibitor treatment

canonical_statement: Type 1 diabetes mellitus was an exclusion criterion in the final protocol.
Ketoacidosis within the previous 5 years was an exclusion criterion.
At randomization, nonadherence to run-in treatment or a qualifying acute event during run-in could exclude a participant from randomization.

population.label: Eligibility criterion
exclusion_criteria: Run-in nonadherence or specified acute event during run-in

canonical_statement: All potentially eligible participants entered a single-blind prerandomization placebo run-in intended to select participants likely to continue study treatment.
Participants randomized to intervention received empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily.
Participants randomized to control received matching placebo once daily.
Randomization used minimization on age, sex, prior diabetes, eGFR, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and region, with a 10% stochastic element.
Follow-up visits occurred at 2 and 6 months and then every 6 months until final follow-up.
At follow-up, sites collected kidney status, adherence and concomitant medications, serious and protocol-specified adverse events, blood pressure, weight, and laboratory safety measures.

Deaths and selected potential clinical events, including heart-failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, stroke, liver injury, ketoacidosis, amputation, acute kidney injury, and serious genital infections, were adjudicated by clinicians blinded to treatment assignment.
Laboratory-defined kidney outcomes were based preferentially on central creatinine measurements, with prespecified substitution of local creatinine measurements when central samples were missing.
The final data-analysis plan was intended to define randomized analyses before unblinding of treatment allocation.
The primary outcome was the first occurrence of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death.

concept.text: Kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death

outcome.definition: First occurrence of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death.

canonical_statement: Kidney disease progression comprised end-stage kidney disease, sustained eGFR below 10 mL/min/1.73 m², sustained eGFR decline of at least 40% from baseline, or renal death.

outcome.definition: ESKD, sustained eGFR <10 mL/min/1.73 m², sustained ≥40% decline from baseline, or renal death.

canonical_statement: End-stage kidney disease was defined as initiation of maintenance dialysis or receipt of a kidney transplant.

outcome.definition: Initiation of maintenance dialysis or receipt of a kidney transplant.

canonical_statement: A qualifying sustained eGFR decline was based on two consecutive scheduled measurements at least 30 days apart or an eligible terminal scheduled measurement under prespecified conditions.

outcome.definition: Two consecutive scheduled measurements at least 30 days apart or specified terminal scheduled measurement.

canonical_statement: Key secondary outcomes were heart-failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death, recurrent all-cause hospitalization, and all-cause death.

outcome.definition: HF hospitalization/CV death; first and recurrent all-cause hospitalization; all-cause death.

canonical_statement: The trial targeted 1070 first primary-outcome events to provide 90% power at a two-sided alpha of 0.05 to detect an 18% lower primary-outcome risk.
A single formal interim efficacy analysis was prespecified when 150 participants had experienced a first ESKD event.

At the interim analysis, early-stopping conditions required a primary-outcome hazard ratio below 0.778 with two-sided P<0.0017 and an ESKD-or-cardiovascular-death hazard ratio meeting its prespecified efficacy condition.
All efficacy analyses were conducted according to intention to treat and included data collected after the formal interim analysis through final follow-up.
Time-to-event hazard ratios were estimated with Cox models adjusted for age, sex, diabetes history, eGFR, urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio, and geographic region.
The three key secondary outcomes were controlled for multiple testing with the Hochberg step-up procedure at a familywise error rate of 0.029.
First and recurrent all-cause hospitalizations were analyzed with a semiparametric joint frailty model.
eGFR slope analyses used shared-parameter models to account jointly for longitudinal eGFR and informative kidney-failure/death events.
A total of 8544 potential participants attended screening, 8184 entered run-in, and 6609 underwent randomization.
Among 6609 randomized participants, mean age was 63.8 years and 33.2% were women.
Among randomized participants, 3569 (54.0%) did not have diabetes.
Mean baseline eGFR was 37.3 mL/min/1.73 m², and 2282 participants (34.5%) had eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m².
Median baseline urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio was 329 mg/g, and 3192 participants (48.3%) had UACR of 300 mg/g or less.
At baseline, 5628 participants (85.2%) were receiving a renin–angiotensin system inhibitor.
The main reported kidney-disease causes were diabetic kidney disease (31.1%), glomerular disease (25.3%), and hypertensive or renovascular disease (21.9%).
Median follow-up was 2.0 years (interquartile range 1.5 to 2.4).
At trial end, 6552 participants (99.1%) had completed final follow-up or died; vital status was missing for 18 (0.3%) and 39 (0.6%) withdrew consent.
At 12 months, 89.6% of empagliflozin-group participants and 90.3% of placebo-group participants reported taking more than 80% of assigned tablets.

On March 7, 2022, the data and safety monitoring committee reported that both prespecified efficacy conditions for early stopping had been met at the formal interim analysis; follow-up was completed July 5, 2022.

The primary composite occurred in 432 of 3304 empagliflozin participants (13.1%) and 558 of 3305 placebo participants (16.9%), corresponding to an adjusted hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI 0.64–0.82; P<0.001).

canonical_statement: Over about 2 years, the primary outcome corresponded to 42 fewer events per 1000 participants assigned empagliflozin than placebo.

concept.text: Kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death

canonical_statement: First and recurrent all-cause hospitalizations occurred at 24.8 versus 29.2 events per 100 patient-years with empagliflozin and placebo, respectively; hazard ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.95; P=0.003).
Heart-failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death occurred in 131 empagliflozin participants (4.0%) and 152 placebo participants (4.6%); hazard ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.67–1.07; P=0.15).

concept.text: Hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death

canonical_statement: All-cause death occurred in 148 empagliflozin participants (4.5%) and 167 placebo participants (5.1%); hazard ratio 0.87 (95% CI 0.70–1.08; P=0.21).
Kidney disease progression alone occurred in 384 empagliflozin participants (11.6%) and 504 placebo participants (15.2%); hazard ratio 0.71 (95% CI 0.62–0.81).
Cardiovascular death occurred in 59 empagliflozin participants (1.8%) and 69 placebo participants (2.1%); hazard ratio 0.84 (95% CI 0.60–1.19).
The composite of ESKD or cardiovascular death occurred in 163 empagliflozin participants (4.9%) and 217 placebo participants (6.6%); hazard ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.59–0.89).
From randomization to final follow-up, empagliflozin reduced the annual eGFR decline by 0.75 mL/min/1.73 m² per year versus placebo (95% CI 0.54–0.96).
From month 2 to final follow-up, the long-term eGFR slope difference favored empagliflozin by 1.37 mL/min/1.73 m² per year (95% CI 1.16–1.59).
The geometric mean urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio was 19% lower with empagliflozin than placebo (95% CI 15%–23% lower).
Weighted-average systolic blood pressure was 2.6±0.3 mm Hg lower with empagliflozin than placebo.
Weighted-average body weight was 0.9±0.1 kg lower with empagliflozin than placebo.
Among participants with diabetes, the primary-outcome hazard ratio was 0.64 (95% CI 0.54–0.77).

canonical_statement: The treatment effect on the primary outcome was generally consistent across prespecified key subgroups, with some evidence of greater proportional benefit at higher baseline albuminuria.
Prespecified exploratory eGFR-slope analyses showed slower chronic eGFR decline with empagliflozin in all key subgroups, including participants with low baseline albuminuria.
Serious urinary tract infection occurred in 52 empagliflozin and 54 placebo participants; hazard ratio 0.94 (95% CI 0.64–1.37).
Serious hyperkalemia occurred in 92 empagliflozin and 109 placebo participants; hazard ratio 0.83 (95% CI 0.63–1.09).
Serious acute kidney injury occurred in 107 empagliflozin and 135 placebo participants; hazard ratio 0.78 (95% CI 0.60–1.00).
Serious dehydration occurred in 30 empagliflozin and 24 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.25 (95% CI 0.73–2.14).
Liver injury occurred in 13 empagliflozin and 12 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.09 (95% CI 0.50–2.38).

Ketoacidosis occurred in 6 empagliflozin participants and 1 placebo participant, corresponding to 0.09 versus 0.02 events per 100 patient-years; one empagliflozin event occurred in a participant without baseline diabetes.
Lower-limb amputation occurred in 28 empagliflozin and 19 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.43 (95% CI 0.80–2.57).
Bone fracture occurred in 133 empagliflozin and 123 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.08 (95% CI 0.84–1.38).
Severe hypoglycemia occurred in 77 participants in each group; hazard ratio 1.00 (95% CI 0.73–1.37).
Symptomatic dehydration occurred in 83 empagliflozin and 76 placebo participants; hazard ratio 1.10 (95% CI 0.81–1.51).
Serious genital infection occurred in 1 participant in each randomized group.
The authors concluded that empagliflozin reduced the risk of kidney disease progression or cardiovascular death in a broad CKD population at risk for progression.
The authors interpreted the trial as extending SGLT2-inhibitor kidney-protection evidence to large numbers of patients without diabetes and to patients with eGFR below 30 mL/min/1.73 m².
The authors reported no major overall safety concerns with empagliflozin in this trial.
The lower-than-expected number of cardiovascular events reduced statistical power for secondary and tertiary cardiovascular outcomes.
Among participants with UACR below 300 mg/g, fewer primary-outcome events limited precision because CKD progressed more slowly in this group.
The final protocol specified centralized monitoring of critical-to-quality factors and maintained an electronic audit trail for entered data changes.
The final protocol permitted treatment discontinuation for specified safety or clinical reasons while follow-up was intended to continue whenever consent allowed.
The final data-analysis plan defined intention-to-treat censoring using the final follow-up visit, death, or last-known-alive/consent-loss information under prespecified rules.
For on-treatment safety analyses, participants who permanently stopped study treatment were censored at the recorded stop date plus 7 days.
The final data-analysis plan prespecified scheduled follow-up analysis windows with ideal visit days, including 2, 6, 12, 18, and 24 months.
